chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Urwa, from Bureyd Al-Ajaly, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'A man died and left his daughter and his uncle.' He said, 'The wealth is for the daughter and there is nothing for the uncle,' or he said, 'There is nothing for the uncle with the daughter.'
ai.seo_question: Does a daughter exclude her uncle from inheritance in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the exclusionary principle (hajb) where a daughter excludes her paternal uncle from inheritance, a key distinction in Shia jurisprudence compared to some Sunni schools. The Imam’s phrasing emphasizes that the daughter’s share is primary and sufficient to preclude the uncle entirely, reinforcing the Quranic allocation of fixed shares (fara'id) as the foundation of distribution. This hadith is frequently cited by scholars like al-Tusi and al-Majlisi to demonstrate the consistency of the Ahl al-Bayt’s understanding of inheritance law with the Quranic text.
